report.tagline: A Bengaluru app that would pick up and drop anything in the city, which became an early 15-minute grocery service and then collapsed by early 2025.
report.simpleSummary: Dunzo started in 2014 as a WhatsApp number: you messaged what you needed, like keys from home or medicine from a shop, and a rider fetched it. It became Bengaluru's favourite errand app and got money from Google and later Reliance. It then switched to 15-minute grocery delivery from its own warehouses, where Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart had far more money and stores. It ran out of cash, stopped paying staff, and shut down; Reliance wrote off its $200 million investment in January 2025.

overview.whatItDoes: Dunzo was a hyperlocal delivery app, meaning it delivered within one city, usually within a few kilometres. Its first product was 'pick up and drop anything' plus buying from nearby shops for you. From about 2020 it ran Dunzo Daily, a quick grocery service from its own dark stores. It no longer operates; the company was taken into insolvency in 2025.
howItWorks: Original model (2014 to 2020): you asked for any errand, a rider bought or picked it up from a local shop and brought it to you, and Dunzo charged a delivery fee.
Dunzo also worked as a marketplace: it listed nearby kirana stores, pharmacies and meat shops, and took a cut of each order.
Dunzo Daily (2020 to 2024): Dunzo ran dark stores, small warehouses near homes, and promised groceries in 15 to 19 minutes.
It also ran B2B delivery for businesses, including for Reliance's JioMart.
From 2023 it cut cities, staff and stores as money ran out, and by early 2025 the app was effectively offline.
overview.valueProposition: At its best: one app that could get anything from anywhere in your city to your door within an hour, and later groceries in about 15 minutes.

businessModel.summary: Dunzo made money from delivery fees and a cut of orders from partner shops. With Dunzo Daily it moved to owning stock and earning a margin on groceries, plus brand ads. It never made a profit.

revenueStreams.detail: Charged on pick-up-and-drop and shop orders.
A cut of orders placed with listed shops.
Difference between buying and selling price of stock.
Fees from businesses including Reliance's JioMart.

businessModel.pricing: Not public now; the service has shut down. Delivery fees used to vary by distance and demand.
costDrivers: Heavy discounts to match Blinkit and Zepto
Large marketing spends, like about ₹40 crore on a 20-second IPL ad in 2022
Technology and a large head office team
businessModel.unitEconomics: Pick-up-and-drop orders were one-off trips with low fees, so one rider made one delivery and earned little per hour; most orders lost money. Dunzo Daily needed each dark store to handle roughly 1,000+ orders a day to cover rent and staff, but Dunzo had only about 120 stores and fewer orders per store than rivals. With discounts of ₹50 to ₹100 on many orders (estimate), it likely lost money on almost every order, which is why losses were many times its revenue.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth in Bengaluru for its unusual 'anything' errands
Witty social media and outdoor ads
Heavy discounts during the quick commerce race
Big TV and IPL ads in 2022
whatBringsUsersBack: Unique errand use cases nobody else served

growth.moat: Dunzo's only real moat was its brand and its 'anything' errand service in Bengaluru. Once it moved into dark-store grocery, it had no edge: rivals had more stores, more money and bigger user bases, so customers switched to whoever was cheapest.

northStar.metric: Completed deliveries per week that arrived on time (what Dunzo should have tracked)
northStar.why: A north star metric is the one number that shows users get value. For a delivery app, a completed, on-time delivery is the value. Tracking it alongside profit per order would have shown the problems sooner.

improvementIdeas.idea: In hindsight: stay focused on errands and local-shop marketplace, and charge for it
improvementIdeas.problem: Dunzo gave up its unique business to fight in a crowded one.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Smaller but more defensible business with lower capital needs.

improvementIdeas.idea: In hindsight: launch dark stores only in a few dense Bengaluru areas first
improvementIdeas.problem: Spreading to 15 cities with 120 stores left each store under-used.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher orders per store and break-even in some stores.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Orders per dark store per day

improvementIdeas.idea: In hindsight: cut discounts and test real demand at full price
improvementIdeas.problem: Discounts hid whether customers valued Dunzo over rivals.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: True retention picture and lower cash burn.

improvementIdeas.idea: In hindsight: set strict cash runway rules and protect salary payments
improvementIdeas.problem: Running out of cash destroyed trust with staff and vendors.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Time to find a buyer or pivot before collapse.

pmLessons: Do not abandon what makes you different. Dunzo's errand service was unique; its grocery service was a copy of richer rivals.
In quick commerce, scale wins. Fixed costs per store mean the player with the most orders per store has the best economics.
Discounts can hide a product problem. Growth bought with cash disappears when the cash stops.
A famous investor does not guarantee survival. Reliance's $200 million did not fix weak economics.
Treat runway as a product metric. A company that cannot pay staff loses its ability to build anything.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Dunzo fail when Blinkit and Zepto succeeded?
interviewQuestions.hint: Cover strategy (left unique errands), scale (120 vs 1,000+ stores), money (funding winter), and execution (stock, pricing errors). End with one key lesson.

interviewQuestions.question: If you were Dunzo's PM in 2021, would you have launched Dunzo Daily?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh market size and threat of rivals vs capital needs and focus. A strong answer suggests a narrow test with clear stop rules.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you have made pick-up-and-drop profitable?
interviewQuestions.hint: Raise prices for urgency, batch nearby orders, sell to businesses, add subscriptions. Track margin per order.

interviewQuestions.question: What early warning metrics would have shown Dunzo was in trouble?
interviewQuestions.hint: Orders per store, repeat rate without discounts, contribution margin, cash runway, vendor payment delays.

interviewQuestions.question: Could Dunzo have been saved in 2023? How?
interviewQuestions.hint: Options: shrink to Bengaluru, sell to a rival, focus on B2B. Compare cash needs and chances. Pick one with reasons.
